definition.text: Whether an intervention, such as a payment or credit, actually causes an outcome that would not have happened anyway, judged against a baseline.

facts.text: A baseline is a prediction of what the actors would do without the policy, holding everything else constant.
It can be checked after the fact, as in programme evaluation, or beforehand, as an eligibility screen for issuing environmental credits.
Additionality is the impact of the intervention minus the impact of a reference case, net of deadweight, leakage, displacement and substitution.
A project is not additional if it would have gone ahead anyway, for example because it is profitable without carbon credits; that scenario is called business as usual.
Biodiversity offsets must show additionality to compensate for losses, and large offset markets have shown serious shortcomings on it.
The Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market cited additionality concerns in excluding several renewable energy crediting methods.
Problems with additionality and double counting can undermine the credibility of carbon offsets.

title: Watershed management

definition.text: The planning and running of programmes that sustain a watershed's functions and share its resources sustainably among its plant, animal and human communities.

facts.text: It covers water supply, water quality, drainage, stormwater runoff and water rights.
On farms it uses buffer strips, grassed waterways, restored wetlands and practices such as conservation tillage and crop rotation.
In towns, retention ponds, filters and wetlands let stormwater soak in so soil and plants filter it before it reaches streams.
Donors backed by the World Bank argue freshwater should be governed as an economic good through pricing, while NGOs see it as a social good.
Groups sharing a watershed often have unequal, divergent interests, so one group's actions can harm others downstream.
Network governance, in which stakeholders form voluntary partnerships, has been adopted by states sharing the Rhine, Nile and Lake Chad basins.

related: New York City water supply system
contested_note: Donor institutions and NGOs disagree over whether freshwater should be managed as an economic good or a social good.

title: Conditional cash transfer

definition.text: Programmes that fight poverty by paying cash only to people who meet conditions, such as sending children to school or getting vaccinations.

facts.text: Few development programmes have been evaluated as rigorously.
By 2011 they had spread to 18 Latin American countries, covering up to 129 million people.
Brazil's Bolsa Família pays poor households if school-age children are enrolled and younger children vaccinated.
Evidence from Mexico and Malawi found conditions raised school enrolment compared with unconditional payments.

notes: Seeded in the PES chapter as a model of conditional payments; the dossier has no sentence linking it directly to PES.
